_about: URL canonicalization policy. The governing principle is: prefer a false negative over a destructive false-positive merge. Keeping two records that turn out to be the same is recoverable — an alias joins them later. Collapsing two records that were actually different destroys information no later step can recover.
_strip_about: Removed unconditionally from every URL. An explicit allowlist of things to STRIP, never a heuristic.
_never_strip_about: Frequently assumed to be tracking and are NOT. Recorded so a future reader does not helpfully add them: '?ref=' selects a content variant on some sites, '?source=' is part of path identity on others, and the rest are ordinary content selectors.
_not_done_about: Operations deliberately NOT performed during string canonicalization, because none is guaranteed identity-preserving. Each is handled only by evidence-based aliasing.

not_done_in_string_canonicalization.scheme_upgrade: http: -> https: requires an observed 301/308, a verified rel=canonical, or a domain_equivalence rule. A 302/307 never rewrites identity.
not_done_in_string_canonicalization.strip_www: Same class of assumption as scheme upgrade. Alias-only.
not_done_in_string_canonicalization.strip_trailing_slash: '/a' and '/a/' are distinct resources in RFC 3986. Alias-only.
not_done_in_string_canonicalization.sort_query_params: Parameter order is content-significant on some sites and repeated keys carry order. Only under a per-domain query_sort rule.
not_done_in_string_canonicalization.strip_fragment: Fragments are preserved by default; see fragment_policy.

_fragment_about: Fragments are PRESERVED by default. Stripped only under an explicit per-domain rule, or with fetched-document evidence that the fragment names an ordinary in-document anchor on a host not configured for hash routing. Structure alone is never sufficient: '#dashboard' is not an anchor merely because it lacks a leading '/' or '!'.

fragment_policy._never_strip_why: Hashbang routes, router paths and query-bearing fragments identify the resource itself.

_domain_rules_about: Per-domain overrides. Each rule must carry a _why documenting the evidence for its safety, and each is covered by its own test. Empty by default — nothing is assumed safe.

example.com._why: Template only. Populate a real entry with the evidence that justified it.

_migration_about: Authorized cross-domain equivalences. A cross-registrable-domain rel=canonical is accepted ONLY with a rule here or independent 301/308 evidence; otherwise it becomes an alias_conflict. A rule here also authorizes merging two already-independent records. Empty by default.
_canonical_trust_about: Trust tiers for a rel=canonical tag. A canonical tag is never trusted merely because it appeared in HTML.
